after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

priority.description: Priority levels, OR-combined; "none" selects tasks with no priority signifier

tag.description: Tag on the task line, "#" optional; matches nested tags, any letter case

heading.description: Exact heading text or array of headings, OR-combined, case-sensitive (e.g. "Active" or ["Active", "Up Next"])

path.description: Restrict to one note (vault-relative path ending ".md", case-sensitive)

top_level_only.description: When true, only top-level tasks (depth 0) are returned — excludes indented sub-tasks and checklist items. Default false.

limit.description: Max results (default 50); total always reports the full match count

sort_by.description: Sort key (default "due"). Date sorts cascade through related fields when the primary is absent (through the rest of due → scheduled → start → created, in that order; done does not cascade). "position" sorts by file path then line number.

sort_direction.description: Sort direction. Default per field: "asc" for due/scheduled/priority/position, "desc" for start/created/done/note_mtime. When a date sort cascades (see sort_by), each field uses its own default direction; an explicit value overrides all fields uniformly.

tools.name: vault_memory_recall
tools.title: Memory Recall
tools.description:
Recall memory entries about a topic — entry-granular hybrid (keyword + semantic) retrieval across ALL About Me/ files and ALL time. Returns the relevant dated entries, up to limit, sorted oldest-first, so the full evolution of a preference, opinion, or fact is visible — semantic matching finds early entries even when their phrasing differs from the query. Tuned for recall over precision: expect some marginal entries. Content-word queries ("testing philosophy", "sustainable pacing") rank best. A meta-framed query ("opinions on testing") that scores below the relevance threshold degrades to any-term keyword matching instead of returning nothing.

Example: vault_memory_recall({ query: "working hours and pacing" })
Example: vault_memory_recall({ query: "testing philosophy", file: "Opinions" })

When to use: Answering "what does my memory say about X?" or "how has my view on Y evolved?" — topic-based recall across memory files. Prefer vault_get_memory to read a known file or section verbatim; prefer vault_search for notes outside the memory layer.

Behavior: A memory file change takes a few seconds to appear here, so an entry written moments ago may not be recalled yet.

Errors:
- No matching entries returns entries: [] and total: 0, not an error
- An unknown file returns empty results — call vault_list_memory_files to discover valid names
- "[SqliteError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON { entries, total, truncated, search_mode, reranked }. Each entry is { file, section, date, text } — text is the raw entry markdown (wikilinks intact, continuation lines included); file and section feed directly into vault_get_memory or vault_delete_memory. The total counts every matched entry; truncated=true means limit dropped the least-relevant matches, whatever their dates, so raise limit or narrow the query for the complete set. The file filter is applied before limit, so limit keeps the most relevant matches from that file. search_mode is "hybrid" when semantic matching contributed and "fts" when keyword matching alone did, the any-term fallback included; reranked is true when the reranker ran.

query.description: Topic to recall, in natural language.

file.description: Restrict to one memory file, name without .md (e.g. "Opinions"), in its exact letter case. Omit for cross-file recall — the default and usual choice.

tools.name: vault_move_note
tools.title: Move Note
tools.description:
Move or rename a note and rewrite every link across the vault that points to it, like Obsidian's built-in rename. Incoming links in other notes — [[wikilinks]], [[wikilink|aliases]], [[wikilink#headings]], ![[embeds]], [markdown](links.md), and frontmatter links (e.g. related:) — and Canvas cards that embed the note are updated to the new path; the moved note's own relative links are fixed so they still resolve from the new folder, including relative links to attachments (e.g. ![[../assets/photo.png]], ![img](../assets/photo.png)). A link is only rewritten when leaving it unchanged would break it, so a short [[Note]] that stays unambiguous after a folder move is left alone.

Example: vault_move_note({ old_path: "Inbox/Draft.md", new_path: "Inbox/Spec.md" }) — pure rename.
Example: vault_move_note({ old_path: "Inbox/spec.md", new_path: "Inbox/Spec.md" }) — case-only rename; works even where the filesystem treats both spellings as one file.
Example: vault_move_note({ old_path: "Inbox/Spec.md", new_path: "Projects/Spec.md" }) — move to another folder.
Example: vault_move_note({ old_path: "Inbox/Spec.md", new_path: "Projects/Spec.md", prune_empty_folders: true }) — also remove "Inbox" if the move empties it.

When to use: Renaming a note or relocating it to a different folder while keeping the link graph intact.
Prefer this over vault_write_note + vault_delete_note, which would orphan every backlink. To only change a note's body or properties, use vault_patch_note or vault_update_properties. Protected paths cannot be moved: About Me/ and the daily notes folder (Daily Notes/ by default; not protected when it is the vault root or blank).

Parameters:
- prune_empty_folders keeps a folder that holds any file, even a hidden .DS_Store. An in-place rename or a move into a subfolder of the source prunes nothing. Pruning is best-effort: a folder that can't be removed never fails the call.

Errors:
- "destination exists: …" — this tool never overwrites; pick a free new_path or delete the existing note first.
- "note not found: …" — old_path does not exist; verify path with vault_list_notes.
- "source and destination are the same path" — nothing to move; pass a different new_path.
- "cannot move protected path …" / "cannot move into protected path …" — old_path or new_path sits under a protected folder; pick a new_path outside it, or leave a protected note where it is.
- "cannot read daily notes config from .obsidian/daily-notes.json" — ask the vault's owner to repair it, or the server operator to set DAILY_NOTES_FOLDER or PROTECTED_PATHS, then retry.
- "path must end in …" — add the .md extension.
- "absolute path blocked" / "path traversal blocked" / "hidden path blocked" — use vault-relative paths with no hidden (dot-prefixed) file or folder in them.
- "concurrent write in progress" — a write is in flight on the note, the destination, or one of its backlink sources; retry the move.
- "backlink set did not stabilize" — notes linking to the note kept changing during the move; nothing was written; retry the move.
- "move aborted: …" — nothing was written. "could not read …" names the note, or a note linking to it, that could not be read; fix that note, then retry. "could not rewrite …" says why a note could not be saved with its links rewritten, and how to fix it. "could not write to …", or "could not rename to …" for a case-only rename, means new_path could not be created (new parent folders it needed may remain); retry once, then ask the vault's owner to fix the folder or disk.
- "move incomplete: …" — the move failed partway; no data is lost, and the message names what failed, the state it left, and the step that finishes the move.
- "ENAMETOOLONG: …", "EACCES: …" or another filesystem error code — the message says what to do; nothing was written.
- "[SqliteError]: …" — the search index failed and nothing was written; the message says what to do.

Obsidian syntax: Link rewrites preserve each link's existing form — embed marker (!), heading anchor (#…), and alias (|…) are kept; a markdown link keeps its original extension and link text.

Returns: JSON with moved_to (the new path), links_updated (count of link occurrences rewritten, including the moved note's own relative links), updated_notes (sorted paths of the other notes and Canvas files that were edited; the moved note is implied by moved_to), and pruned_empty_folders (count of empty parent folders removed).

old_path.description: Current vault-relative path of the note to move (e.g. "Inbox/Draft.md"). Must end in .md. Use the exact letter case.

new_path.description: Destination vault-relative path (e.g. "Projects/Spec.md"). Must end in .md; parent folders are created as needed. Use the exact letter case of existing folders; a different case can create a second folder.

prune_empty_folders.description: When true, also remove parent folders of old_path that the move leaves empty. Default false.

tools.name: vault_patch_note
tools.title: Patch Note
tools.description:
Surgical edits to a markdown note — append, prepend, replace, or insert content by heading. Properties are kept as written, and CRLF line breaks are saved as LF.

Example: vault_patch_note({ path: "Projects/plan.md", operation: "append", heading: "Open questions", content: "- Which region hosts the backup?" })
Example: vault_patch_note({ path: "Notes/Plan.md", operation: "replace", heading: "Status", content: "On track for launch.\n" })
Example: vault_patch_note({ path: "Notes/Plan.md", operation: "insert_before", heading: "Phase 2", content: "## Phase 1\nDone.\n" })
Example: vault_patch_note({ path: "Notes/Plan.md", operation: "prepend", content: "> [!info] Draft\n> Not reviewed yet.\n" })

When to use: Modifying part of an existing note without overwriting the entire body.
Prefer vault_write_note for creating new notes, or full rewrites (with overwrite: true). Prefer vault_replace_in_note for in-place text changes (typos, renaming) that stay in the same location. Prefer vault_insert_at_anchor for inserting next to a specific line inside a section. Prefer vault_replace_span for replacing a run of lines inside a section. Prefer vault_delete_span for removing lines. Prefer vault_update_properties for changing frontmatter properties. Prefer vault_create_task for adding a task. Prefer vault_update_task for completing or moving a task in one write.

Operations:
- append: add content at end of section (or end of file if no heading), below any empty lines that end it, so appending a row to a table that a blank line follows starts a new table; to extend a table, use vault_insert_at_anchor after its last row
- prepend: add content after heading line (or at the top of the body, below frontmatter, if no heading — how you add a leading callout). To start a new section above the note's current first heading, use insert_before on that heading: a no-heading prepend whose content starts with a heading nests any content above the first heading inside the new section.
- replace: replace section body (requires heading); to empty it, use vault_delete_span on its lines
- insert_before: insert content above the heading line (requires heading)

Heading-targeted ops keep the matched heading. Every operation writes content verbatim as whole lines with no separator: end content with a newline to leave a blank line after it; without one, the next line follows directly.

Section boundaries: a section spans from its heading to the next heading of the same or higher level (or EOF), so it includes its child headings. Empty headings ("##" with no text) act as boundaries but cannot be targeted — edit their content via vault_replace_in_note instead.

Editing a leading callout: read it via vault_read_note(outline: true), then vault_replace_in_note the old block for the new one (a no-heading prepend would stack a second callout above it).

Errors:
- "note not found" — path does not exist; check vault_list_notes for valid paths
- "path must end in …" — add the .md extension
- "heading not found" — the message lists the available headings
- "ambiguous heading" — multiple headings match; use heading_level to disambiguate; if they share a level, rename one or use vault_replace_in_note to target by text content
- "operation … requires a heading target" — pass heading, or use append or prepend to edit the file body
- "heading cannot be empty" — heading is whitespace only; pass the heading's text
- "content begins with the heading … which would duplicate it" — content's first line repeats the target heading; omit it
- "section … has N child headings …" — the target section contains child headings that replace would destroy; pass include_children: true to confirm, or target the child heading directly
- "absolute path blocked" / "path traversal blocked" / "hidden path blocked" — use a vault-relative path with no hidden (dot-prefixed) file or folder in it
- "concurrent write in progress" — another write to this note is in flight; re-read the note and retry
- "content contains a control character" — remove the character the message names
- "ENAMETOOLONG: …", "EACCES: …" or another filesystem error code — the message says what to do
- "the note would open with a properties block …" — the edit would leave --- lines at the top of a note with no properties, around text that can't be kept as properties; the error says how to avoid it

Obsidian syntax: Content is Obsidian Flavored Markdown (no escaping applied). Watch for: #word = tag, [[ = wikilink, %% = comment block.
Table rows: send only the data row ("| cell1 | cell2 |"), not the header or separator — duplicating them splits the table.

Returns: Confirmation message — "Applied <operation> to <path> → <target>", where target is the matched heading (e.g. "## Active") or "file body" for a no-heading append/prepend. A no-heading prepend that nested existing content under an inserted heading adds a sentence naming the content's size and any call that would have avoided it.

path.description: Vault-relative path to the note, including the ".md" extension (e.g. "TASKS.md", "Projects/plan.md"). Use the exact letter case.

content.description: Markdown content to insert, or the section's new body for replace.

heading.description: Target heading text (case-sensitive exact match). Omit for a file-level append or prepend.

heading_level.description: Heading level (1-6) for disambiguation when multiple headings share the same text

include_children.description: When true, allows replace to overwrite a section that contains child headings.

tools.name: vault_read_note
tools.title: Read Note
tools.description:
Read a markdown note by its vault-relative path. By default returns the full raw content including properties; optional modes return just the properties, just the heading outline, or just one section.

Example: vault_read_note({ path: "Projects/vault-cortex.md" })
Example: vault_read_note({ path: "TASKS.md", outline: true })
Example: vault_read_note({ path: "TASKS.md", heading: "Active" })
Example: vault_read_note({ path: "TASKS.md", heading: "Done", heading_level: 2 })
Example: vault_read_note({ path: "TASKS.md", heading: "Done", start_line: 1, limit: 20 })

When to use: You know the exact path and need a specific note's content. For a large note (a long Kanban board or doc), use outline: true to see its headings and any text sitting above them, then heading: "..." to read just the one section you need. For a note or section too long for one response (this tool sets no cap), page it with start_line and limit to read a window at a time. To check a note's or section's line count, request start_line: 1 with limit: 1 — one line plus the total.
Prefer vault_search when you don't know the path. For task status or order on a board, prefer vault_list_tasks; heading mode returns a lane's Markdown. Prefer vault_get_memory for About Me/ files (returns content without properties). To edit a section you've read, use vault_patch_note. To explore what links to this note or what it links to, use vault_get_backlinks and vault_get_outgoing_links.

Section boundaries: a section spans from its heading to the next heading of the same or higher level (or EOF). Child headings are included.

Errors:
- "note not found" — no note exists at this path; verify it with vault_list_notes
- "heading not found" — the message lists the available headings
- "ambiguous heading" — multiple headings match; use heading_level to disambiguate, or read the full note (omit heading) when headings share the same level
- "outline, heading, and properties_only are mutually exclusive — set at most one"
- "heading_level requires a heading" — pass heading with it
- "heading cannot be empty" — heading is whitespace only; pass the heading's text
- "line paging is not available in outline mode" / "… properties_only mode" — start_line and limit page only a full read or a heading section
- "start line past the end" — the message states the line count; resend a start_line within it
- 'path must end in ".md"' — add the extension to a note's path
- "absolute path blocked" / "path traversal blocked" / "hidden path blocked" — use a vault-relative path with no hidden (dot-prefixed) file or folder in it
- "properties block is not valid YAML …" — a full read, outline and heading still work; the error says how to repair it
- "ENAMETOOLONG: …", "EACCES: …" or another filesystem error code — the message says what to do

Returns: Raw markdown string (default); JSON object of properties, {} when the note has none (properties_only); JSON outline object, shaped as the outline parameter describes (outline); raw markdown of the section, heading line included (heading). When start_line or limit is given, the result is preceded by a window-metadata text block ("path — lines 1–20 of 250 (continue with start_line: 21)"). Unpaged full reads return the file's exact bytes; heading sections and paged reads use LF line endings.

Outline: bytes at the root is the whole file's size and modified is its modification time (ISO 8601); each heading's bytes is the size of the text that heading mode returns for that section. Empty headings ("##" with no text) appear with text: "" — they act as section boundaries but cannot be targeted by the heading parameter; read the parent section or the full note, and edit via vault_replace_in_note.

path.description: Vault-relative path to the note, including the ".md" extension (e.g. "About Me/Principles.md"). Use the exact letter case.

properties_only.description: If true, returns parsed properties as JSON instead of full note content

outline.description: If true, returns { bytes, modified, leading_callout?, leading_content?, headings } as JSON instead of body content. headings: [{ level, text, bytes }]; leading_callout: { type, title, body } when the note has a top-of-file callout; leading_content: the rest of the body text above the first heading (callout lines excluded) when the note has any.

heading.description: Return only this section. Case-sensitive exact match.

heading_level.description: Heading level (1-6) for disambiguation when multiple headings share the same text

tools.name: vault_recent_notes
tools.title: Recent Notes
tools.description:
List recently modified or created notes, sorted by timestamp — a time-ordered window into the vault, not a date-range filter.

Example: vault_recent_notes({ sort_by: "modified", limit: 10 })
Example: vault_recent_notes({ sort_by: "created", limit: 5 })

When to use: Catching up on vault changes, finding recent work, or orienting after a break.
Prefer vault_search for content-based discovery, including a text query limited to a date range (its created and modified filters). Prefer vault_search_by_folder for browsing a specific folder.

Parameters:
- sort_by + limit interact: "modified" uses filesystem mtime, which every note has. "created" uses the frontmatter created property; notes without a valid one sort after every dated note, so a small limit can leave them out — use "modified" to see them.
- sort_by "modified" includes any file write (content edits, property changes, sync touches), so recently-synced notes appear recent even without user edits.

Behavior: A file change takes a few seconds to appear here, so a note written moments ago may not be listed yet.

Errors:
- An empty vault returns an empty array, not an error.
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of note metadata (path, title, tags (the tags property, which vault_update_properties edits), body_tags (the #tags written in the note's text, each spelling once, edited as text with vault_replace_in_note; absent when there are none), related, folder (top-level folder), type, created, modified, bytes, leading_callout, additional_properties), newest first. The created field is null when the property is missing or not an ISO date; bytes is on-disk file size. A leading_callout field appears only when the note has one; additional_properties only when frontmatter has keys outside title, type, created, related, and tags.

tools.name: vault_replace_in_note
tools.title: Replace in Note
tools.description:
Find and replace exact text in a markdown note's body. Properties are kept as written — edit them via vault_update_properties or vault_write_note's properties parameter. CRLF line breaks are saved as LF.

Example: vault_replace_in_note({ path: "Projects/plan.md", old_text: "TODO: write summary", new_text: "Summary complete." })
Example: vault_replace_in_note({ path: "Projects/plan.md", old_text: "- [ ] draft outline\n", new_text: "" })
Example: vault_replace_in_note({ path: "Projects/plan.md", old_text: "Q3", new_text: "Q4", replace_all_occurrences: true })

When to use: Targeted text changes within a single location — fixing typos, updating values, renaming terms, or removing a short line (new_text="").
To delete a large multi-line block, prefer vault_delete_span (short anchors instead of full old_text). To replace a large block by anchors instead of reproducing the full old_text, use vault_replace_span. To relocate content between headings, use vault_patch_note to add at the target first, then remove from source (new_text="") — add-before-delete, so a failure duplicates the block instead of losing it.

Parameters:
- old_text: include enough surrounding context to ensure uniqueness when the target text appears in multiple places.
- new_text: a non-empty value replaces the match exactly. For a deletion (new_text=""):
  - When text remains on the line, it is written exactly as asked.
  - When the line empties, blank lines never double: the text above and below is separated by the wider of the two runs of empty lines that stood there, and by at least one. At the note's end the run above counts one fewer ("A\n\nB\n" without "B" → "A\n").
  - To remove a table row or list item, include its line break in old_text, or the empty line left behind splits the table or list.
  - Empty lines elsewhere in the note stay as they are, and a line holding only spaces or tabs counts as text, not as an empty line.
- replace_all_occurrences: set true for deliberate bulk renames or term replacements.

Errors:
- "note not found" — path does not exist; check vault_list_notes for valid paths
- "path must end in …" — add the .md extension
- "text not found" — old_text does not appear in the note body; verify exact text with vault_read_note
- "absolute path blocked" / "path traversal blocked" / "hidden path blocked" — use a vault-relative path with no hidden (dot-prefixed) file or folder in it
- "concurrent write in progress" — another write to this note is in flight; re-read the note and retry
- "new_text contains a control character" — remove the character the message names
- "ENAMETOOLONG: …", "EACCES: …" or another filesystem error code — the message says what to do
- "the note would open with a properties block …" — the edit would leave --- lines at the top of a note with no properties, around text that can't be kept as properties; the error says how to avoid it

Obsidian syntax: new_text is Obsidian Flavored Markdown (no escaping applied). Watch for: #word = tag, [[ = wikilink, %% = comment block in replacement text.

Returns: "Replaced <N> occurrence(s) in <path>".

path.description: Vault-relative path to the note, including the ".md" extension (e.g. "Projects/plan.md"). Use the exact letter case.

old_text.description: Exact text to find, no regex (case-sensitive).

new_text.description: Replacement text. Empty string ("") deletes the matched text.

replace_all_occurrences.description: Replace all occurrences (default: false — replaces first occurrence only)

tools.name: vault_replace_span
tools.title: Replace Span
tools.description:
Replace a contiguous block of whole lines in a note's body with new content, identified by short anchor substrings instead of the block's full text. Properties are kept as written, and CRLF line breaks are saved as LF.

Example: vault_replace_span({ path: "Tracker.md", start_anchor: "| 2024-03-02 | Acme", content: "| 2024-03-02 | Acme Corp | Updated |" }) — replaces the one table row whose line contains that fragment.
Example: vault_replace_span({ path: "Notes/Plan.md", start_anchor: "> [!warning] Stale", end_anchor: "remove after launch", content: "> [!info] Current\n> Updated for v2." }) — replaces the callout block with a new one.

When to use: Replacing a block you have already read — a table row, callout, or run of list items — where reproducing it exactly as old_text would be error-prone.
Prefer vault_replace_in_note for small in-place text changes (typos, renaming). Prefer vault_delete_span when removing without replacement.

Parameters:
- end_anchor is searched at or after the start line and must be unique among those lines. If start_anchor and end_anchor match the same line, only that one line is replaced. A span that includes a code block's opening fence can't end at a plain closing fence (```): the end anchor is ambiguous, and first_match: true would end the span at the opening fence; to replace such a block, use vault_replace_in_note.
- content's line breaks:
  - A line break at its start or end merges with the note's empty lines on that side, keeping the wider run. At the note's end, its trailing line breaks count one fewer.
  - Content ending in a line break ("| X |\n") leaves an empty line after it, which splits a table.
  - Empty lines inside content and elsewhere in the note are kept as written, and a line holding only spaces or tabs counts as text, not as an empty line.

Errors:
- "note not found" — verify path with vault_list_notes
- "path must end in …" — add the .md extension
- "start anchor not found" / "end anchor not found" — no body line holds the fragment where it is searched; verify with vault_read_note
- "ambiguous start anchor …" / "ambiguous end anchor …" — the anchor matches multiple lines; use a longer fragment or set first_match: true
- "absolute path blocked" / "path traversal blocked" / "hidden path blocked" — use a vault-relative path with no hidden (dot-prefixed) file or folder in it
- "concurrent write in progress" — another write to this note is in flight; re-read the note and retry
- "content contains a control character" — remove the character the message names
- "ENAMETOOLONG: …", "EACCES: …" or another filesystem error code — the message says what to do
- "the note would open with a properties block …" — the edit would leave --- lines at the top of a note with no properties, around text that can't be kept as properties; the error says how to avoid it

Obsidian syntax: content is Obsidian Flavored Markdown (no escaping applied). Watch for: #word = tag, [[ = wikilink, %% = comment block.

Returns: Confirmation message "Replaced <N> line(s) with <M> line(s) in <path>" — N counts the lines the span covered, M the lines in content as sent (its line breaks plus one).

path.description: Vault-relative path to the note, including the ".md" extension (e.g. "Tracker.md", "Notes/Plan.md"). Use the exact letter case.

start_anchor.description: Short, unique substring of the block's first line, a body line (case-sensitive).

end_anchor.description: Short substring of the block's LAST line, a body line (case-sensitive). Omit to replace just the single line containing start_anchor.

first_match.description: If an anchor matches more than one line, use the first match instead of erroring (default: false — ambiguity is an error).

tools.name: vault_search
tools.title: Search Notes
tools.description:
Hybrid search across vault notes, ranked by combined keyword and semantic relevance. Semantic matching finds notes even when exact keywords differ — "career aspirations" finds notes about "goals" and "targets". Unquoted terms use implicit AND with stemming ("running" also matches "run"); wrap in double quotes for exact phrases; punctuated terms (vault-cortex, deploy/local) are matched as exact adjacent-word phrases.

Filters — all conditions AND-combine with each other and the text query:
- folder: a whole folder, subfolders included — "Projects" covers "Projects/Archive" but not "ProjectsOld/"; ignores ASCII letter case
- tags: every listed tag must match, in the tags property or as a #tag in the body, in any letter case; "project" also matches "project/a"
- properties: keys and text values match exactly, letter case included; values compare by exact type — pass a number as a number, not "4". Exception: true and false compare as 1 and 0, so true or 1 matches a checked checkbox and the number 1. A list property matches when any element equals the value.
- created / modified: bounds compare whole calendar days in the server's time zone (returned created and modified values show its UTC offset), so "on" matches anywhere within the day. Notes without a parseable created property never match a created filter

Example: vault_search({ query: "how the server watches for file changes" })
Example: vault_search({ query: "kubernetes networking", filters: { tags: ["reference"] } })
Example: vault_search({ query: "meeting notes", filters: { type: "meeting", folder: "Work" } })
Example: vault_search({ query: "decision", filters: { modified: { after: "2026-06-30" } } }) — matching notes touched in July or later

When to use: The primary discovery tool for content-based queries, optionally constrained by metadata.
Prefer vault_search_by_tag for tag-only queries without text. Prefer vault_search_by_folder for browsing a folder. Prefer vault_search_by_property for metadata-only queries. Prefer vault_recent_notes for time-based browsing.

Behavior: Results can lag a file change by a few seconds, so a note written moments ago may not be found yet.

Errors:
- No matches returns an empty results array with total 0, not an error
- Malformed query syntax never throws: the words AND, OR, NOT and NEAR in any letter case, and punctuation such as *, ^, parentheses and colons, are dropped before keyword matching; a query left with no terms is matched by meaning only, or finds nothing when only keyword matching ran (search_mode "fts")
- "invalid created.on date: …" or "… is not a calendar date" (any created/modified bound) — pass a real calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form
- "tag must not be empty …" — a tags entry is only "#"; pass the tag name
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON with results array (path, title, snippet, score, tags (the tags property, which vault_update_properties edits), body_tags (the #tags written in the note's text, each spelling once, edited as text with vault_replace_in_note; absent when there are none), folder (top-level folder), type, kind, created, modified, bytes), total (results returned, not all matches), search_mode ("hybrid" when vector embeddings contributed, "fts" when only keyword matching ran), and reranked (true when reranking refined the ordering). A higher score is more relevant. The kind field is always "note". The created field is omitted, not null, when a result has none; type is null when the result has no type property. The bytes field is the on-disk file size. With include_leading_callout, each result also carries leading_callout ({ type, title, body }) when present.

related.description: Require all listed related links, each written exactly as in the note's related property, brackets and alias included (e.g. "[[Projects/alpha|Alpha]]")

type.description: Match the frontmatter type field (exact, case-sensitive match, e.g. "person", "meeting")

properties.description: Match arbitrary frontmatter properties by key-value (e.g. { status: "active", priority: 1 })

created.description: Created date bounds (YYYY-MM-DD) on the frontmatter "created" property

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

modified.description: Modified date bounds (YYYY-MM-DD) on filesystem modified time

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

snippet_tokens.description: Snippet length in words, not model tokens (default 30)

include_leading_callout.description: If true, include each result's leading callout.

tools.name: vault_search_by_folder
tools.title: Search by Folder
tools.description:
Browse notes in a folder with full metadata.

Example: vault_search_by_folder({ folder: "Projects" })
Example: vault_search_by_folder({ folder: "About Me", recursive: false, limit: 10 }) — the folder's own notes, 10 most recent

When to use: Exploring a folder's contents with full context for vault orientation.
Prefer vault_list_notes when you only need paths. Prefer vault_search when you have a text query. Use vault_get_backlinks or vault_get_outgoing_links to explore how notes in a folder connect to the rest of the vault.

Parameters:
- folder names a whole folder, not a text prefix: "Projects" matches notes under "Projects/" but not "ProjectsOld/". Matching ignores ASCII letter case, and a trailing slash is ignored.
- limit applies after sorting, so you get the most recently modified notes. There is no offset, and nothing in the response signals truncation; raise limit to see more.

Behavior: Results can lag a file change by a few seconds: a note written moments ago may not appear yet, one renamed or deleted moments ago may still be listed, and a just-changed note may show its old metadata. Notes in hidden (dot-prefixed) folders never appear.

Errors:
- An empty or nonexistent folder returns an empty array, not an error.
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of note metadata sorted by most recently modified, then by path: path, title (file name without .md when missing or not text), tags (the tags property, which vault_update_properties edits), body_tags (the #tags written in the note's text, each spelling once, edited as text with vault_replace_in_note; absent when there are none), related ([] when missing), folder (top-level folder), type (null when missing or not text), created (frontmatter; null when missing or not an ISO date), modified (file time), bytes (on-disk size), plus, when present, leading_callout (the note's opening callout, { type, title, body }) and additional_properties (other frontmatter keys).

tools.name: vault_search_by_property
tools.title: Search by Property
tools.description:
Find notes where a frontmatter property matches a value.

Example: vault_search_by_property({ key: "status", value: "in-progress" })
Example: vault_search_by_property({ key: "type", value: "session-log", folder: "Code Projects" })

When to use: Finding notes by metadata when you don't have a text query.
Prefer vault_search when you also have a text query (it supports property filters too). Prefer vault_search_by_tag for tag-specific queries (it matches nested tags and #tags in note bodies; key "tags" here matches only the tags property). Use vault_list_property_keys to discover valid keys and vault_list_property_values to see what values a key takes.

Parameters:
- key matches exactly and case-sensitively; value matches stored text the same way, with no partial matching or globbing.
- A value written as a complete, finite YAML number (-4, 04, .5, 4., 1e3, 0x1F, 0o17) also matches stored numbers numerically: "04" and "4.0" match number 4 and their own literal text, but not text "4". Anything else ("4abc", " 4", 0b binary) matches only as text.
- value for a checkbox: pass "1" (checked) or "0" (unchecked); a checkbox matches only as text, so "1.0" and "true" do not match.
- value against a list property: an element must equal value in full: "blog" matches tags: ["blog", "draft"] but not tags: ["my-blog"].
- folder names a whole folder and includes its subfolders: "Projects" covers "Projects/Archive" but not "ProjectsOld/". Matching ignores ASCII letter case; omit folder to search the entire vault.
- limit keeps the most recently modified matches; nothing in the response signals truncation.

Behavior: Results can lag a file change by a few seconds: a note written moments ago may not match yet, and one changed moments ago may still match its old value.

Errors:
- An unknown key or unmatched value returns an empty array, not an error.
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of note metadata (path, title, tags (the tags property, which vault_update_properties edits), body_tags (the #tags written in the note's text, each spelling once, edited as text with vault_replace_in_note; absent when there are none), related, folder, type, created, modified, bytes, leading_callout?, additional_properties?), sorted by filesystem mtime descending, then by path — recently-synced notes may sort ahead of older content edits.
- folder is the top-level folder ("" at the vault root); title falls back to the file name without .md when missing or not text; related is [] when missing; type is null when missing or not text; created is null when missing or not an ISO date.
- leading_callout appears only when the note has a leading callout.
- additional_properties appears only when frontmatter has keys outside title, type, created, related, and tags.

tools.name: vault_search_by_tag
tools.title: Search by Tag
tools.description:
Find notes by tag, in the tags property or as a #tag in the body, ignoring letter case. Unless exact is true, a tag also matches every tag nested under it at any depth: "project" matches "project/vault-cortex" and "project/a/b". A nested tag continues with "/", so "project" never matches "projects" or "my-project".

Example: vault_search_by_tag({ tag: "project" })
Example: vault_search_by_tag({ tag: "project", exact: true, limit: 50 }) — notes tagged "project" itself, up to 50

When to use: Tag-only lookups, for one tag or a whole tag hierarchy, with no text query. Use vault_list_tags first to discover available tags.
Prefer vault_search when you need text-based relevance ranking.

Parameters:
- limit applies after sorting, so you get the most recently modified notes; nothing in the response signals truncation.

Behavior: Results can lag a file change by a few seconds: a note written moments ago may not appear yet, and one moved, deleted, or retagged moments ago may still be listed.

Errors:
- An unknown tag or no matches returns an empty array, not an error.
- "project/" matches neither "project" nor "project/a"; drop the "/".
- "tag must not be empty …" — tag is "#" alone; pass the tag name.
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the search index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of notes sorted by most recently modified, then by path ascending. Each note has path, folder (top-level folder; "" at the vault root), bytes (on-disk size), modified (file modification time), tags (the tags property, which vault_update_properties edits), body_tags (the #tags written in the note's text, each spelling once, edited as text with vault_replace_in_note; absent when there are none), both in the note's letter case, and the frontmatter values title (file name without .md when missing or not text), related ([] when missing), type (null when missing or not text), and created (null when missing or not an ISO date). Timestamps are ISO 8601. When present, a note also has leading_callout (the callout opening its body, as { type, title, body }) and additional_properties (every other frontmatter key).

exact.description: Match only the tag itself (default: false)

tools.name: vault_update_memory
tools.title: Update Memory
tools.description:
Append a dated entry to a section of a memory file in About Me/. An exact duplicate (same date + text in the same section) is a no-op, so retrying a timed-out call is safe. Memory files are append-only by default: when a preference changes, append the new state (newest wins) rather than deleting the old one. A file may declare `entry-policy: living` in frontmatter (surfaced by vault_list_memory_files) — a current-state file where pruning expired entries with vault_delete_memory is expected maintenance.

Example: vault_update_memory({ file: "Opinions", section: "Code patterns (newest first)", entry: "Prefer immutable data structures" })
Example: vault_update_memory({ file: "Routines", section: "Daily/weekly rhythm (newest first)", entry: "Gym Mon/Wed at 6am", options: { date: "2026-10-01", position: "bottom" } }) — a backdated entry placed below the existing ones

When to use: Recording a new preference, principle, opinion, or fact about the user. Call vault_list_memory_files first and reuse existing file and section names so entries stay grouped.
Prefer vault_write_note for creating non-memory notes. A missing file or section is created automatically.

Parameters:
- options.date only sets the bullet's date; placement follows options.position, never the date.

Obsidian syntax: Entry text is Obsidian Flavored Markdown. Watch for: #word = tag, [[ = wikilink. Escape with \# or backticks when unintentional.

Errors:
- "entry must be a single line" / "section must be a single line" — the message names the fix.
- "date must be a real ISO calendar date" — pass options.date as an existing calendar date in bare YYYY-MM-DD form, not a timestamp.
- "entry contains a control character" / "section contains a control character" — remove the character the message names.
- "memory file must not start with a dot" / "memory file must be a bare name without path separators" / "memory file must be named without .md" — each message names the part of the name to drop
- "section not created: … is nearly identical to existing section …" — pass the exact existing heading (listed in the error) to append there, or choose a clearly different name for a new section.
- "cannot read memory file …" — the file can't be read: check file against vault_list_memory_files and shorten an over-long name; otherwise ask the vault's owner to fix its permissions
- "cannot write memory file …: that path is not a file" — a folder already has this name; choose another file name
- "ENAMETOOLONG: …", "EACCES: …" or another filesystem error code — the message says what to do
- "cannot create memory folder …" — a file sits where the memory folder belongs; ask the vault's owner to move it
- "memory file …: the note would open with a properties block …" — saving would turn the file's opening lines into a properties block the server can't keep; the error says how to avoid it

Returns: "Added entry to About Me/<file>.md → ## <section>", plus a note to fill in the placeholder scope callout when the file is new; an exact duplicate returns "Entry already exists in About Me/<file>.md → ## <section> — nothing was written."

file.description: Memory file name without .md (e.g. "Principles"). Use the exact letter case; a different case can create a second file.

section.description: H2 section heading (e.g. "Decision heuristics (newest first)"). Matched case-insensitively, with or without the "(newest first)" suffix.

entry.description: Raw entry text — a single line, without the "- **YYYY-MM-DD**: " prefix, which the server prepends.

date.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD date (defaults to today, server timezone)

tools.name: vault_update_properties
tools.title: Update Properties
tools.description:
Update a note's frontmatter properties. By default they merge shallowly — new keys added, matching keys overwritten, null deletes a key, unmentioned keys preserved. With replace: true they replace the whole properties block (here null writes an empty property, and {} removes it). The body is kept; a merge only adds a missing final newline.

Example: vault_update_properties({ path: "Projects/todo.md", properties: { status: "active", draft: null } })
Example: vault_update_properties({ path: "Projects/todo.md", properties: { title: "Todo", status: "active" }, replace: true })

When to use: Changing tags, status, type, or any property without reading/rewriting the full note body.
Prefer vault_write_note when creating a new note, or replacing the body (with overwrite: true). Read current properties first with vault_read_note({ properties_only: true }), or the full note when repairing a block. Arrays are replaced entirely, not appended to.

Errors:
- "note not found" — path does not exist; create the note first with vault_write_note
- "path must end in …" — add the .md extension
- "absolute path blocked" / "path traversal blocked" / "hidden path blocked" — use a vault-relative path with no hidden (dot-prefixed) file or folder in it
- "concurrent write in progress" — another write to this note is in flight; re-read the note and retry
- "ENAMETOOLONG: …", "EACCES: …" or another filesystem error code — the message says what to do
- "properties block …" — without replace: true, the merge refuses a block it cannot keep: invalid YAML, a list, a single value, or a YAML tag; the error says how to repair it
- "the note would open with a properties block …" — the edit would leave --- lines at the top of a note with no properties, around text that can't be kept as properties; the error says how to avoid it

Obsidian syntax: Use arrays for multi-value fields (tags: [a, b]), quote wikilinks ("[[Note]]"), keep types consistent (mismatches cause silent query failures).

Returns: "Updated properties on <path>", or "Replaced properties on <path>" with replace: true.

path.description: Vault-relative path to the note, including the ".md" extension. Use the exact letter case.

properties.description: Properties to merge, or with replace the complete new set.

tools.name: vault_update_task
tools.title: Update Task
tools.description:
Update a task's status, priority, description, dates, recurrence, completion action, dependencies, block_id, checklist items, heading, or position within a lane, in any combination; every field passed is written in a single edit.

Example: vault_update_task({ path: "TASKS.md", block_id: "my-task", status: "done" }) — complete a task; on a Kanban board, auto-moves to the done lane
Example: vault_update_task({ path: "TASKS.md", block_id: "my-task", recurrence: "every week" }) — make a task recurring
Example: vault_update_task({ path: "TASKS.md", block_id: "my-task", heading: "Done" }) — move a task to a different heading (the checkbox is unchanged)
Example: vault_update_task({ path: "TASKS.md", block_id: "my-task", description: "Updated task name", due: "2026-10-01", scheduled: null }) — change the description, set one date, and clear another
Example: vault_update_task({ path: "TASKS.md", block_id: "my-task", status: "in_progress", add_subtasks: ["Design", "Implement", "Test"] }) — start working and add checklist stages
Example: vault_update_task({ path: "TASKS.md", line: 42, assign_block_id: "my-task" }) — add a block_id to a task that lacks one

When to use: Any change to an existing task. Use vault_list_tasks first to get identification fields (path + block_id or line). For creating a new task, use vault_create_task instead.

Parameters:
- Exactly one of block_id or line is required to identify the task. A Kanban sub-task this server created has no block_id, so re-read its line with vault_list_tasks just before an update by line. After a write, wait a few seconds for the listing to catch up.
- At least one change is required. Clearing is always explicit null — omitting a field leaves it untouched.
- status side effects:
  Kanban: "done" moves the card and everything nested under it to the done lane (the lane whose first line is **Complete**, else the heading "Done", exact case), leaving nested checkboxes as they are; a sub-task stays under its parent.
  Recurring (🔁), on "done" only: spawns the next occurrence, dates advanced per the rule, directly above the completed task, which keeps its nested lines. When the Tasks plugin's settings put the next recurrence on the line below, the spawn goes on the line directly below the task instead, so the task's nested lines then sit under the spawn. The spawn stays in the source lane with no block_id, 🆔, or ⛔ — follow up with assign_block_id on next_occurrence.line, except on an indented line of a Kanban board. Completing by line is NOT idempotent for recurring tasks (the spawn occupies the old line); prefer block_id.
  Delete (🏁 delete / [onCompletion:: delete]), on "done": removes the task line and its children instead of moving to done. With 🔁 + 🏁, the next occurrence is still created, and the completed task is removed.
- recurrence: a rule ending "when done" bases the next occurrence on the completion day. When set together with status "done", the new rule governs the next occurrence. Setting recurrence to null while completing removes the rule and completes without spawning.
- on_completion: passed together with status, the submitted value governs the delete decision — "keep" while completing a "delete" task prevents the deletion.
- position: applies to a heading move or an auto-done-lane move; otherwise it reorders the task within its current lane. Omitted, an unmoved task stays put. Ignored when the task is deleted on completion.

Errors: (messages use camelCase names, e.g. assignBlockId for assign_block_id)
- "note not found" — path does not exist; check the path with vault_list_notes
- "path must end in …" — add the .md extension
- "absolute path blocked" / "path traversal blocked" / "hidden path blocked" — use a vault-relative path with no hidden (dot-prefixed) file or folder in it
- "exactly one of blockId or line is required" / "blockId and line are mutually exclusive" — the message states the rule
- "blockId ... not found" / "blockId ... is inside a fenced code block or comment" — no task line outside a fenced code block or %% %% comment ends with that ^id; check the id with vault_list_tasks, or target by line
- "blockId ... matches N task lines" — more than one task line ends in the id (the message lists their line numbers); target the intended task by line. To repair on a regular note, give all but one line a new id with assign_block_id. On a Kanban board, where the plugin copied a sub-task's id onto its card, remove the id from the sub-task's line (assign_block_id: null, by line), then assign the card the id its existing links use, or a new one
- "no task at line N" / "line N is inside a fenced code block or comment" — the line holds no task checkbox, or sits inside a fenced code block or %% %% comment; re-read line numbers with vault_list_tasks, or target by block_id
- "checkbox "[c]" is a NON_TASK status" / "no checkbox symbol for status ..." — in the Tasks plugin's status settings, the targeted task's checkbox character (c) is typed NON_TASK so it is not a task, or the status the message names has no symbol and its default character has another type; the user must change that character's type or add a symbol for that status there, then restart the server
- "at least one mutation" — the message lists the fields that count
- "cannot move a sub-task to a heading" / "cannot reposition a sub-task" — a heading or position on a task nested under another task (depth > 0 in vault_list_tasks); sub-tasks move with their parent, so move or reposition the parent instead
- "cannot reorder a task that sits above the first heading" — position without a heading on a task before the first section heading; the message names the fix
- "cannot reorder within "X" — the heading appears N times" / "cannot place at position P under "X" — the heading appears N times" — the heading name is duplicated in the note: the task's own heading for a reorder in place, the one in heading for a move; for a cross-lane move use "top" or "bottom" (they place under the first match), or rename one section to make it unique
- "heading "X" not found; available: ..." — the message lists the note's headings
- "multiple done lanes detected" / "no done lane detected" — status "done" on a Kanban board with more than one lane whose first line is **Complete**, or with none and no "Done" heading; pass heading to pick the lane
- "blockId ... already exists" / "blockId ... contains invalid characters" — assign_block_id must be unique in the note and match [a-zA-Z0-9-]+
- "assignBlockId is not allowed" / "description ends in a block ID" / "subtask ... ends in a block ID" — a new ^id on an indented line of a Kanban board; leave the line without an id and target it by line, and drop any trailing ^id from the text
- "invalid date: …" — the message names the expected format
- "description cannot be empty" / "addSubtasks cannot contain an empty item" / "description must be a single line" / "addSubtasks items must be a single line" — pass visible text on a single line
- "taskId ... contains invalid characters" / "dependsOn entry ... contains invalid characters" — the message names the allowed characters
- "unrecognized recurrence rule ..." — the message gives example rules
- "concurrent write in progress" — another write to this note is in flight; retry
- "ENAMETOOLONG: …", "EACCES: …" or another filesystem error code — the message says what to do
- "properties block …" — the note's properties block can't be read, or a rewrite would lose it; the error says how to repair it
- "the note would open with a properties block …" — the edit would leave --- lines at the top of a note with no properties, around text that can't be kept as properties; the error says how to avoid it

Obsidian syntax: When description or add_subtasks text ends in a signifier the plugin's parser recognizes as a field (an emoji field like "🔁 every week", or a Dataview [key:: value] field), with only other recognized fields after it, that text is read back as metadata, not text. The write still succeeds either way; reword the text to clear any advisories the result carries. The ✅/❌ dates a status change adds or removes produce no advisories by themselves.

Returns: JSON { path, line, description, block_id, heading, subtasks, next_occurrence, changes, advisories, on_completion_applied }.
- line is the task's final 1-based line number in the file; after an on_completion delete, the line the task occupied before removal.
- description is the current text, and block_id and heading reflect the task after the update; block_id is omitted when the task has none, heading when the task sits above the first heading.
- subtasks lists each checklist item add_subtasks wrote as { line, description } (omitted when none were added); checklist items are written without a block_id, so line is the handle for a follow-up update.
- next_occurrence is present only when a completion spawned a recurring task's next occurrence: { line, description, due?, scheduled?, start? } with only the dates the occurrence has.
- changes lists every field applied as "field: before → after", with "(none)" for an absent value; an add_subtasks change is listed under "subtasks", a spawn under "next_occurrence", and a 🏁 delete under "on_completion".
- advisories (omitted when there are none) lists one sentence for each: a stored line that parses back differently than submitted (see Obsidian syntax above), a duplicate tag removed from the line, or a completed recurring task whose rule yields no next occurrence (unreadable rule text, or a finite rule with no occurrences left).
- on_completion_applied is "delete", present only when the effective on_completion was delete (already on the task or set in the same call) and the task was transitioned to done.

path.description: Vault-relative path to the note containing the task (must end in ".md"). Use the exact letter case.

block_id.description: Stable task identifier — the ^block-id at the end of the task line, without the ^. Preferred over line.

line.description: 1-based line number from vault_list_tasks. Fragile if the file changed since the query.

status.description: Target status. "done" adds the ✅ date and "cancelled" the ❌ date, when the Tasks plugin's settings stamp them; moving a task out of either status removes its date.

priority.description: Priority signifier to set, or null to remove it.

recurrence.description: Tasks plugin 🔁 rule in natural language (e.g. "every week", "every month on the 15th", "every 2 weeks when done") to set, or null to remove it.

on_completion.description: Tasks plugin 🏁 onCompletion action to set, or null to remove it. "keep" leaves the task in place on completion, as having no 🏁 field does.

description.description: New task description text; metadata fields and block_id are preserved.

due.description: Due date (YYYY-MM-DD) to set, or null to clear.

scheduled.description: Scheduled date (YYYY-MM-DD) to set, or null to clear.

start.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD) to set, or null to clear.

created.description: Created date (YYYY-MM-DD) to set or clear, for corrections. vault_create_task stamps it on every new task.

task_id.description: Tasks plugin 🆔 identifier to set, or null to clear — letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores; separate from block_id.

depends_on.description: Tasks plugin ⛔ dependency IDs to set (non-empty), or null to clear.

add_subtasks.description: Checklist items to append, one indented todo line each, under the task's existing items. Not appended, and not reported, when the same call removes the task (on_completion delete). For full sub-tasks with metadata, use vault_create_task with parent_block_id.

assign_block_id.description: Add or replace the ^block-id on the task line, or null to remove it. Letters, digits, and hyphens only; must be unique within the note.

heading.description: Target heading to move the task to. On Kanban boards this is a lane move; works on any note with headings. Not valid on sub-tasks.

position.description: Where within the target heading the task lands. "top" or "bottom" for the extremes; an integer (1-based) for an exact position among the lane's top-level cards (sub-tasks move with their parent and are not counted). A position past the card count lands directly below the last card (unlike "bottom", which appends after any non-task text at the end of the section). Defaults to "top" on heading and done-lane moves.

format.description: Field format for metadata this call writes; fields it leaves alone keep theirs, so a line can mix formats. Default: auto-detected from .obsidian/ config, falling back to emoji.

tools.name: vault_write_note
tools.title: Write Note
tools.description:
Create a markdown note, or with overwrite: true replace an existing note's body; the old body's text is lost unless the new body includes it. Properties merge with any existing properties when overwriting (new keys added, matching keys overwritten, keys set to null removed, unmentioned keys preserved); overwriting without properties keeps the existing property values. A new note leaves out keys set to null.

Example: vault_write_note({ path: "Projects/notes.md", body: "# Notes\n\nProject notes here.", properties: { tags: ["project"], type: "project" } })
Example: vault_write_note({ path: "Projects/notes.md", body: "Updated content.", overwrite: true })

When to use: Creating a new note, or replacing a whole note's body.
Prefer vault_patch_note or vault_replace_in_note to change part of a note.
Prefer vault_update_properties for property-only edits (no body round-trip).
Prefer vault_update_memory for appending dated entries to About Me/ memory files.

Errors:
- "note already exists" — set overwrite: true to replace it
- "path must end in …" — add the .md extension
- "cannot write note …: that path is not a file" — a folder already has this name; choose another path
- "absolute path blocked" / "path traversal blocked" / "hidden path blocked" — use a vault-relative path with no hidden (dot-prefixed) file or folder in it
- "concurrent write in progress" — another write to this note is in flight; re-read the note and retry
- "body contains a control character" — remove the character the message names
- "ENAMETOOLONG: …", "EACCES: …" or another filesystem error code — the message says what to do
- "properties block …" — with overwrite: true, the note's properties block can't be read, or a rewrite would lose it; the error says how to repair it
- "the note would open with a properties block …" — the edit would leave --- lines at the top of a note with no properties, around text that can't be kept as properties; the error says how to avoid it

Obsidian syntax: Body is Obsidian Flavored Markdown (no escaping applied). Watch for: #word = tag (escape with \#), [[ = wikilink, %% = comment block. In properties: quote wikilink values ("[[Note]]"), use YAML lists for tags, keep property types consistent (string/number/list mismatches cause silent query failures).

Returns: "Wrote <path>".

path.description: Vault-relative path including the ".md" extension (e.g. "Projects/notes.md"). Parent folders are created as needed. Use the exact letter case; a different case can create a duplicate note or folder.

body.description: Markdown body content — do not include frontmatter fences (---); use the properties parameter instead.

overwrite.description: Allow overwriting an existing note (default: false).
